mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals robust labor market conditions and expanding economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 50,000 jobs month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 5.0%, it indicates a tight labor market that typically precedes stronger consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE is below 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in consumer credit demand (RSAFS) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong economic expansion, which typically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as market participants anticipate sustained growth.
failure_condition: The interaction between RSAFS and INDPRO shows a Rank IC below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window, or positive 60-day returns occur in less than 40% of periods when both series rise.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, rising federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) compress equity valuations by increasing discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods classified as monetary tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.0%, it signals aggressive monetary policy that typically triggers equity market sell-offs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) reflects strong consumer confidence and economic activity, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the housing sector drives broader economic growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST increases by at least 10% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it signals persistent inflation that typically prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY change exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime, a sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 indicates severe supply constraints that typically lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate margins contract.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO falls below 100 in the past 3 months.
